proxy_input: Why can bald people still grow beards?
target_output:
That’s a great observation! The reason bald people can often still grow beards comes down to how hair follicles in different parts of the body respond to hormones—specifically **dihydrotestosterone (DHT)**.

Here’s the simple breakdown:

- **DHT is a powerful androgen** (male sex hormone) made from testosterone.
- Scalp hair follicles (especially on the top and front of the head) are **genetically sensitive to DHT**. In those areas, DHT causes hair follicles to shrink over time, producing thinner, shorter hairs until they stop growing altogether—this is male pattern baldness.
- **Beard hair follicles react the opposite way.** They are **stimulated by DHT** to grow thicker, darker, and more robust. That’s why during puberty, when testosterone and DHT levels rise, facial hair begins to develop.

So essentially, baldness and beard growth are two sides of the same hormonal coin—it all depends on how the hair follicles are programmed to respond to DHT. Genetics determine which scalp follicles are sensitive to balding and how robust your beard growth becomes. That’s why you can see a completely bald man with a full, thick beard.
